Now, one question I've gotten quite a bit
is whether we can leverage world models and video generation

And we've seen some really impressive results, especially
recently from video generation models,
where they clearly have a lot of rich knowledge about the world,

So it seems like this sort of knowledge

But there's actually a lot of nuance
and a lot of challenges with using these kinds of models.
As an example, if you train an action-conditioned video
generation model--
so a model that takes as input the current image
and future actions and predicts future video--
and if you train that on demonstrations and rollouts
from one policy and then you evaluate a new policy's
actions with that model and evaluate whether or not that
those actions lead to good outcomes,
then these actions won't necessarily
be represented in the data that the model was trained on.
And as a result, the model often will make inaccurate predictions
for these actions.
If most of the data set is demonstrations,
then it will predict a video that
corresponds to correctly doing the task
even if these actions did not lead to a correct outcome.
And generally, these models have very little data--
for example, like narrowly making a mistake
or making mistakes that are very different from the kinds
of mistakes that humans make.
The other thing here is that even small physical inaccuracies
can lead to poor performance.
And so a lot of times, these videos look really, really good.
They look like they might be accurate.
But that doesn't mean that the underlying physics is actually
accurate.
Now, I think that there are solutions here.
One possible solution is to try to train
on data from lots of different policies
with this kind of approach, with the hopes
that that will lead to enough coverage over action
distributions to leverage these models.
And then the second possible solution

should the future video look like not conditioned on actions?

And something like this kind of sidesteps the challenge
of this sort of out-of-distribution action
problem because you're only using
the model for a form of planning where you're thinking
through what is a good outcome in the future

is the outcome of specific actions.
And then the third thing on the method side--
the third challenge that I'll talk about

So on the scaling front, we've seen large-scale RL

As another example, if we think about reasoning

So towards this end, if we wanted
